_instructions: Copy this file to ~/.claude/settings.json (or merge it into your existing one).
Replace every <ROOT> placeholder with the absolute path to your workspace root.
Replace <YOUR-TRACKER-HUB-PATH> with the absolute path to your tracker hub (on a single-repo start this is simply <ROOT>/Claude).

Replace <YOUR-USER> in the deny rules with your OS user name. The deny examples cover the common credential stores and browser profile data on Windows, macOS, and Linux together; entries for platforms you are not on match nothing and are safe to keep or trim. Deny rules use gitignore-style patterns; a leading // anchors at the filesystem root.
The Stop hook passes the write-back gate its two paths via env vars on the command line - filling THIS file configures that gate completely; the script-level placeholders are a backstop only.

The git gate lives at hooks/git-gate.mjs and fails closed; it quotes your hard lines from hooks/hard-lines.txt, so put your push and commit constraints in that file (or let the rules interview write them for you).

The env block caps runaway loops. The harness defaults are 200 subagent spawns and 200 web searches per session; the template ships 25 spawns, 50 searches, 10 concurrent subagents, and a spawn depth of 1. Raise them per-session for a sanctioned big run ($env:CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION = '100' before launching) instead of raising the standing cap.
The CLAUDE_REVIEWED allow rules let a git command the git gate blocked, once verified and re-issued with that prefix, run without a second permission prompt.

The directory gate warns when a folder added mid-session (/add-dir) is one of your excluded workspaces, and re-states the rule layers when it is outside your root; list your excluded paths in hooks/dir-added-gate.mjs.
The reply gate enforces a prose-length ceiling on each turn's final reply (default 300 words; REPLY_GATE_MAX_WORDS overrides). It blocks once with exact findings, then always passes the revision.

The token reporter prints each turn's full token spend (subagents included) as a systemMessage line and appends a daily JSONL ledger under ~/.claude/token-ledger/. The token handoff surfaces the previous turn's cost inside the next reply, for hosts that do not render systemMessage output; if your host renders it, the handoff is optional.

Premium-tier subagent spawns run without an approval prompt by default; add an ask rule (for example Agent(model:opus)) per premium tier if you want one - the env caps below bound the runaway class either way.
The hooks block is the governance wiring; preference settings regenerate from use.
The git gate's command detection is regex-based and best-effort - a speed bump, not a security boundary; pair it with permission rules for anything that must be impossible.
